reproduction:
Local HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8890 that answers any GET with 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK' + Content-Length: 5 and body '-foo-'. Then:
  printf '# only a comment line' > netrc
  curl --netrc --netrc-file ./netrc http://127.0.0.1:8890/
At parent_commit this dies with 'Segmentation fault' (exit 139). At fix_commit it exits 0 and writes the server body to stdout. The .netrc file contains only a comment (a file with no machine/login entries has the same effect).
observed_failure_at_parent: Segmentation fault (SIGSEGV, shell reports 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)', exit code 139). Golden run: tests/runtests.pl -n 2429 reports 'FAIL 2429: use netrc file with only comments' / 'protocol FAILED!' because curl crashes while loading the netrc file, before connecting. Buggy code confirmed at parent: lib/netrc.c netrc_scan_file() calls netrc_scan() with an empty (NULL-content) dynbuf; comment lines are skipped during load so a comment-only file leaves the buffer empty, and netrc_lexer_next() dereferences the NULL content pointer (`switch(*s)`). The fix's empty-buffer guard (`if(!curlx_dyn_len(filebuf)) return NETRC_NO_MATCH;`) is absent at parent (grep count 0).
verified: Both directions observed in container on bench-base:ubuntu-24.04, curl built from source (autoreconf + ./configure --with-openssl --enable-debug, OpenSSL 3.0.13). Parent fd8c409d: CLI repro segfaults (exit 139); golden test 2429 (fix-file overlaid) FAILS. Fix 1143bc9a: CLI repro exits 0 and downloads the body; golden test 2429 PASSES (1/1 OK, 100%). Buggy code presence: dyn_len guard count 0 at parent, 1 at fix. Verified once with a non-debug build and again after a clean --enable-debug rebuild; identical results.

apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential autoconf automake libtool pkg-config perl openssl libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libpsl-dev libzstd-dev libbrotli-dev strace
cd /work && git config --global --add safe.directory /work && autoreconf -fi && ./configure --with-openssl --enable-debug && make -j$(nproc)
(cd tests && make all)   # needed only to run the project test harness
Clone with full history (git clone https://github.com/curl/curl.git), then git reset --hard <sha> between runs.
issue_paraphrase: When curl is told to read credentials from a .netrc file that contains only comments and no real machine entries, the whole program crashes with a segmentation fault immediately on startup, before any connection is attempted. The crash happens while the credential file is being parsed: an empty parsed result is fed into the tokenizer, which reads from a null pointer. Any script that passes --netrc together with such a comment-only (or effectively empty) credentials file dies instantly instead of simply finding no matching login and continuing anonymously. The failure is deterministic and does not depend on the requested URL or reachable network.
fix_summary: netrc_scan_file() returns NETRC_NO_MATCH before calling netrc_scan() when the accumulated file buffer is empty, avoiding the NULL-content dereference in the tokenizer. Added test 2429 (comment-only .netrc without trailing newline) that previously crashed curl and now completes a plain HTTP request.
notes: Fully offline (only a loopback HTTP server needed). Reproduction of the crash needs no special build; for the project's own test 2429 the test harness must be built (make -C tests all) and run via tests/runtests.pl -n 2429. The golden test only needs the plain HTTP (sws) test server. Debug build recommended but not required for this entry (verified in both). Netrc file needs no trailing newline for the crash; a multi-line comment-only file also crashes.

reproduction:
Local HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8891 answering any GET with:
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2010 14:49:00 GMT
  Content-Length: 5
  Connection: close
  Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=1152921504606846976
(and body '-foo-'). Seed the cache file, then:
  printf '# Your HSTS cache. https://curl.se/docs/hsts.html\n# This file was generated by libcurl! Edit at your own risk.\nsomehere.example "20330525 03:33:20"\nelsewhere.example.com "20330727 03:33:20"\n' > hsts_in
  CURL_HSTS_HTTP=yes CURL_TIME=1920582000 curl -s -o /dev/null --hsts ./hsts_in --resolve this.hsts.example:8891:127.0.0.1 http://this.hsts.example:8891/
  wc -c < hsts_in
At parent_commit hsts_in is truncated to 0 bytes (all cached entries destroyed and the new host never recorded). At fix_commit it is 228 bytes and contains the original two entries plus 'this.hsts.example "20321109 23:00:00"' (max-age capped at two years). Requires a --enable-debug build: the CURL_HSTS_HTTP env override that allows plain-HTTP HSTS processing is honored only under DEBUGBUILD.
observed_failure_at_parent: The entire --hsts cache file is wiped: after the request, hsts_in is 0 bytes (verified with `wc -c` and strace: hsts_in opened O_WRONLY|O_TRUNC by Curl_fopen for mode cloning, temp file written partially then unlinked because hsts_out() fails to format the 2^60-second expiry with curlx_gmtime). Golden run: tests/runtests.pl -n 1862 FAILS at parent ('FAIL 1862: HSTS with extreme max-age', expected file content missing; diff shows all three entries '-'). Buggy code confirmed at parent: lib/hsts.c parses max-age with limit TIME_T_MAX (grep 'CAP_HSTS_MAX_AGE' count 0) and hsts_out() returns an error that aborts the whole Curl_hsts_save() loop.
verified: Both directions observed in container on bench-base:ubuntu-24.04 with a --enable-debug build (debug build is REQUIRED for this repro because CURL_HSTS_HTTP is #ifdef DEBUGBUILD in lib/http.c; earlier non-debug attempt silently skipped HSTS processing and was correctly identified as an environment miss). Parent b8172ada: CLI repro leaves hsts_in at 0 bytes (exit 0 but cache destroyed); golden test 1862 (fix-file overlaid) FAILS. Fix 08d50a79: CLI repro leaves 228-byte file with capped entry this.hsts.example "20321109 23:00:00"; golden test 1862 PASSES (1/1 OK). Buggy code presence: CAP_HSTS_MAX_AGE count 0 at parent, 3 at fix; gmtime-failure path exercised at parent per strace.

issue_paraphrase: A server that sends a Strict-Transport-Security response header with an extremely large max-age value (anything well beyond the roughly two-year cap that browsers apply) makes curl destroy the on-disk HSTS cache it maintains: after the request finishes, the file holding the remembered secure-only hosts has been truncated to zero bytes, so all previously cached hosts are forgotten and the current server is not recorded either. The damage happens when curl writes the cache back at exit: the oversized expiry cannot be converted to a calendar date, the write aborts, and the cache file has already been emptied by then. One such response disables the user's HSTS memory entirely until the cache is rebuilt, and the numeric value in the header does not even need to overflow - it just needs to exceed what the date formatter can represent.
fix_summary: Curl_hsts_parse() now caps max-age at 2*365*24*3600 seconds (and treats anything larger as capped instead of keeping an unrepresentable expiry), and hsts_out()/Curl_hsts_save() no longer abort the whole save when a single entry cannot be formatted - a broken entry is skipped and the rest of the cache is still persisted. Added test 1862 with max-age=2^60 and a fixed fake clock verifying the capped entry is written while pre-existing entries survive.
notes: Debug build mandatory (CURL_HSTS_HTTP override and the harness's <features>Debug</features> both require it). Deterministic with CURL_TIME=1920582000 (fixed fake clock, so the capped date output is exactly '20321109 23:00:00'); without it the file still ends up correct but with a now+2y date. Needs only a loopback HTTP server. Golden test 1862 needs the harness build (make -C tests all) and runs in ~1s. The CURL_TIME env var can be set in the invocation; the golden test sets it via <setenv>.

reproduction:
Minimal IMAP server on 127.0.0.1:8893 (python3) that answers CAPABILITY, AUTHENTICATE/LOGIN, SELECT (with UIDVALIDITY 3857529045), FETCH and LOGOUT and prints every client command to transcript.log. Then:
  curl -s -o /dev/null -u user:secret \
    'imap://127.0.0.1:8893/Private/;MAILINDEX=123/;SECTION=1' \
    'imap://127.0.0.1:8893/private/;MAILINDEX=456/;SECTION=2.3'
  grep -c 'SELECT' transcript.log
At parent_commit the transcript contains exactly ONE SELECT ('A003 SELECT Private') and then a bare 'FETCH 456' - the second request reuses the mailbox selected for the first despite the case-different name. At fix_commit the transcript contains TWO SELECTs ('A003 SELECT Private' and 'A005 SELECT private') - the server receives a proper SELECT before the second fetch. grep -c must yield 1 at parent (fail) and 2 at fix (pass).
observed_failure_at_parent: Two IMAP URLs in one invocation differing only by mailbox-name case result in a single SELECT on the wire: transcript shows 'A003 SELECT Private / A004 FETCH 123 BODY[1] / A005 FETCH 456 BODY[2.3] / A006 LOGOUT' - the second fetch is executed against the previously selected mailbox. Golden run: tests/runtests.pl -n 804 with the fix's version of tests/data/test804 FAILS at parent ('804: protocol FAILED', diff shows missing '-A005 SELECT private'). Buggy code confirmed at parent: lib/imap.c imap_perform() selects on curl_strequal() (case-insensitive) so 'Private' == 'private'; the strcmp-based exact match (with INBOX exception) is absent at parent (grep count 0).
verified: Both directions observed in container on bench-base:ubuntu-24.04, curl built from source. Parent 81787b0b: standalone repro transcript has 1 SELECT; golden test 804 (fix test-file overlaid onto parent) FAILS with 'protocol FAILED'. Fix 12cfc836: standalone repro transcript has 2 SELECTs; golden test 804 PASSES (1/1 OK, 100%). Buggy code presence: '!strcmp(imap->mailbox' count 0 at parent, 1 at fix. curl exit code is 0 in both directions - the bug is silent wrong-mailbox access, which is why the transcript check (or the golden test) is the observable.

issue_paraphrase: When two IMAP URLs are fetched in a single curl invocation and their mailbox paths differ only in letter case, the second request silently skips the re-selection step and runs its fetch against the mailbox that was selected for the first request. Case is significant to IMAP servers, so 'Private' and 'private' can be completely different folders, yet the client assumes they are the same and never issues the second SELECT command. As a result, mail is read from the wrong folder without any error or warning being reported, and only the raw command transcript (or a strict server) reveals that the wrong mailbox was addressed. Mixed-case folder names on the same server connection are sufficient to trigger it.
fix_summary: imap_perform() now compares the requested mailbox with the connection's currently selected mailbox case-sensitively (with an explicit case-insensitive exception only for 'INBOX'), so a case-differing mailbox name forces a new SELECT before the FETCH. test804 was updated to request 'Private' then 'private' and verify two SELECT commands on the wire.
notes: Fully offline: the standalone repro needs only the small python IMAP server (approximately 50 lines, included in the reproduction field of this entry's verification above; the harness's ftpserver.pl is a reference implementation of the needed responses). The task must assert on the server-side transcript (count of SELECT commands), not on curl's exit code (0 in both directions). Golden test 804 needs the harness build and an 'imap' server - runtests.pl starts one automatically from tests/ftpserver.pl. Compare with real case differences in the mailbox; identical names must still reuse the selection, so a naive 'always SELECT' fix is wrong.
